title: Incremental token latency allocation and cache impact tracing
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: We need fine-grained instrumentation that attributes latency and cost to incremental token emission steps and isolates the effect of KV/prefix cache hits and misses. Current observability aggregates request-level timings which obscures cache economics and prevents per-customer unit-cost reconciliation for sequences with mixed cache behavior.

Goals:
- Emit stable, low-cardinality traces and metrics that break a single request into ordered emission spans (token_index, phase) so we can correlate per-token latency with cache state and kernel selection.
- Surface cache impact: capture whether each emission span was served from local KV, hot remote cache, cache miss (backend recompute), or prefilled prefix.
- Produce metrics streams usable by billing/reconciliation and by console dashboards: per-token latency distributions by model/variant, request-type, and cache outcome.
- Enable sampling that preserves head/tail behavior for long sequences while capping cardinality for high-throughput customers.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing billing pipeline changes in this ticket; this is instrumentation and observability only.
- Not adding new kernel-level timers inside third-party runtimes (we will integrate if they expose hooks).

Design and approach:
1) Trace span model: introduce ordered emission spans named "emit:<i>" where <i> is the token emission index. Each span contains low-cardinality tags: model, variant, host_pool, cache_outcome (hit_local|hit_remote|miss|prefill), emission_phase (kv_lookup|compute|kernel_exec|serialize), token_index_bucket (head/1-16|mid/17-256|tail/257+), and request_id. We will avoid literal token text or token ids in traces.

2) Metrics: For each emission span we will increment counters and record histograms: emit_latency_ms, kv_lookup_ms, compute_ms, kernel_ms, and a gauge emit_cache_outcome. Histograms are configured for high-resolution at head tokens and coarser at tail. Metrics keys are templated to collapse by model and cache_outcome to keep cardinality manageable.

3) Sampling and aggregation: To avoid explosion, full emission-span tracing is enabled for 0.5% of requests by default with deterministic sampling for known customers. We will also provide a per-customer toggle for increased sampling. Aggregation pipeline will roll token_index into buckets and produce daily rollups used by billing.

4) Logging: For sampled traces we will add structured logs linking spans to request-level metadata (customer_id, route, pinned_model). Logs redact any PII and do not include prompt contents.

5) Pipeline and storage: Traces flow into our APM backend (currently X-APM), metrics to Prometheus+THANOS, and aggregated artifacts to the metrics warehouse for further joins with billing traces. We will add a transformation job that tags aggregated token-bucket latency by cache_outcome.

6) Dashboards and alerts: Create console dashboards with breakdowns: per-model emit latency by token_bucket and cache_outcome, and tail-latency P99 per-route. Alerts on spike in cache_miss_ratio or P99_emit_latency exceeding SLOs.

Success criteria:
- Instrumentation emits emission spans for >=99% of sampled requests with correct cache_outcome tag.
- Console dashboard shows token-bucketed latency and cache miss ratio for runtime-1.24 models.
- Aggregated metrics available in warehouse for billing reconciliation jobs.
- No customer-visible latency regression from tracing (<0.5ms median overhead on sampled path).

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1: API design and low-level trace/span schema review with runtime and infra teams.
- Week 2: Add emission spans in runtime codepath with cache_outcome tagging and initial metrics; unit tests.
- Week 3: Hook downstream pipeline (APM + metrics) and create aggregation job; mammoth-run tests on staging.
- Week 4: Create dashboards and run 2-week shadow sampling for verification, then enable deterministic sampling for a set of pilot customers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cardinality blowup: mitigate with token_index_bucket, emission_phase, and strict label set; enforce cardinality quotas in APM.
- Overhead: keep sampling conservative; ensure timers are lightweight and avoid locks on hot path.
- Data joins for billing: coordinate with billing team to ensure trace IDs are persisted in warehouse.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Incremental+Emission+Tracing
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9421 (WIP)
- Draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/token-latency-cache-impact

Next steps: finish runtime PR, add metrics config, wire pipeline transformer, and schedule design review with Security for log redaction rules.
acceptance_criteria: Emission spans emitted for sampled requests with cache_outcome tag present
Metric emit_latency_ms and kv_lookup_ms available in Prometheus for models on runtime-1.24
Dashboard in Console replicates per-token-bucket latency and cache miss ratio
Sampling overhead measured and below 0.5ms median on sampled path
Aggregation job produces daily rollups consumable by billing team
